title: Guide
subtitle: How music is added, played and managed in the library.

start.title: First steps
start.where: applies the first time the application is opened.
start.figure: The toolbar at the top of the library: this is where the music comes in the first time.
start.tip: A library already exported from another installation is imported from {settings} → Library, without starting from the folders again.

sections.title: Adding the music
sections.text: {addFolder} brings in a whole folder and its subfolders in a single operation.

sections.title: Playing a track
sections.text: {gesture} on a track starts playback. The displayed list becomes the playback queue.

sections.title: Customizing the application
sections.text: {settings}, in the title bar, gathers the language, the appearance and the player behavior.

import.title: Adding tracks and folders
import.where: top bar of the Library, or by dropping onto the window.
import.figure: The commands that add tracks and folders.
import.tip: The files stay where they are: when a folder is moved after the import, its tracks read as missing until they are imported again from the new place.

sections.title: Choosing files or folders
sections.text: {addFiles} opens the choice of one or more audio files, {addFolder} imports all the music in a folder and its subfolders. Files and folders can also be dropped onto the window: the library lights up to say it is ready for them.

sections.title: Supported formats
sections.text: Formats read: MP3, FLAC, M4A, OGG and WAV.

sections.title: Result of the import
sections.text: The same file never enters twice: one already in the library is counted among the skipped ones. A summary then says what was added, what was already there and what could not be imported; a clean import closes itself.

organize.title: Searching, filtering and sorting
organize.where: top bar, column headers and library menu.
organize.figure: The search field and the library menu, with the filters and the tools.
organize.tip: Sorting, searching and filtering never touch the files: they only change the way the list is shown.

sections.title: Finding a track
sections.text: The search field filters the list by title, artist, album, genre or path.

sections.title: Order of the list
sections.text: A click on a column header sorts the list; a second click on the same column turns the order around. In the preview views, which have no headers, the order is chosen from the sort control beside the view switch.

sections.title: Missing metadata
sections.text: "Missing data", in the library menu, leaves on screen only the tracks without a cover, an artist, an album, a year or a genre.

views.title: Views, tabs and connections
views.where: the two icons on the right of the bar, and the tabs under it.
views.figure: The switch between list and cards, at the end of the toolbar.
views.tip: The view, the size of the cards and the layout of the columns are remembered separately for each tab.

sections.title: Ways of browsing
sections.text: The list icon shows the columns, the grid icon shows the covers; the choice is remembered. The Tracks, Artists, Albums and Genres tabs gather the same library in four ways.

sections.title: Related tracks
sections.text: A click on an artist, an album or a genre opens the window of the tracks connected to it. The button at the top left of that window goes back, and names where it lands.

sections.title: Columns of the list
sections.text: Which columns the list shows, and in which order, is set from "Columns" in the library menu.

metadata.title: Editing the metadata
metadata.where: the three dots menu on the row or on the card, or a right click on the row.
metadata.figure: The three-dot menu on the row of the track.
metadata.tip: An edit over many tracks is safer once a single one has been tried: the change is written into the files and cannot be undone.

sections.title: Opening the editor
sections.text: The three dots menu, like a right click on the row, holds the Edit entry. Title, artist, album, year and genre can be changed; the genre can be picked among the ones already in the library or typed. "Choose image…" replaces the cover (PNG or JPEG, up to 5 MB).

sections.title: Saving to the files
sections.text: {save} writes the changes into the tags of the file, not only into the library. A field left empty removes that value from the file.

sections.title: Editing several tracks at once
sections.text: With several tracks selected through {ctrl} or {shift}, "Edit selected" appears: it writes the same value on all of them.

files.title: Working on the files
files.where: library menu and the three dots menu on the row.
files.tip: A file reported missing that still exists has almost always been moved: it is imported again from its new place, and the old entry removed.

sections.title: Checking the missing files
sections.text: "Check files", in the library menu, runs the check on request and says how many are missing. A track whose file is gone can be neither edited nor played, but stays listed until it is removed.

sections.title: Finding duplicates
sections.text: "Find duplicates" lists the tracks held in more than one file, matched by title with its artist or by file name.

sections.title: Removing from the library
sections.text: "Delete", in the row menu, takes the track out of the list without deleting anything from the disk.

player.title: Listening to the music
player.where: double click a row or a card; the player appears at the bottom.
player.figure: The player along the bottom, with the controls and the progress bar.
player.tip: Stop rewinds without emptying the queue: the track starts again from the beginning.

sections.title: Starting playback
sections.text: {gesture} on a track starts playback. The displayed list becomes the playback queue.

sections.title: Playback controls
sections.text: {play} and {pause} govern the listening. The progress bar is dragged to seek within the track, while the slider sets the volume. Shuffle and Repeat one change how the queue plays.

sections.title: The full player
sections.text: The arrow at the top right of the player opens the full view, the X closes the playback. In that view artist, album and genre are links: they open the connected tracks, from which another one can be started.

dock.title: Floating player
dock.where: appears when the app goes to the system tray while something is playing.
dock.figure: The floating player and its controls.
dock.tip: The place the floating player was left in is remembered: it comes back where it was.

sections.title: Listening in the background
sections.text: The low dash button, in the title bar, sends the app to the system tray: the playback carries on. With a track playing, the floating player appears: a small window with cover, title and controls.

sections.title: Position and orientation
sections.text: It is moved by dragging it from any free spot. Its menu turns it between horizontal and vertical, and decides whether it stays above other windows.

sections.title: Back to the library, or closed
sections.text: The expand button brings the application back on screen and closes the floating player. Closing it asks whether to quit the application or leave it in the system tray: the answer can be remembered.

shortcuts.title: Shortcuts and gestures
shortcuts.where: the track list, the player and the detail windows.
shortcuts.tip: The search field works on title, artist, album, genre and path at once: one word is usually enough to narrow the list.

sections.title: Playback and menus
sections.text: Double-click on a row or on a card: playback starts. Right-click on a row: the same menu as the three dots opens.

sections.title: Selection and keyboard
sections.text: {ctrl} + click adds a track to the selection, {shift} + click takes the whole range. {esc} closes the open window and, from the full player view, returns to the library.

sections.title: Dragging
sections.text: Dropping files or folders on the window imports them without going through the buttons. Dragging the edge between two headings changes the width of a column; the command next to the gear fits them to their content.

libraries.title: More than one library
libraries.where: the two arrows icon beside the name, and {settings} → Library.
libraries.figure: The two-arrow icon next to the name of the library.
libraries.tip: The primary library is the one that opens at launch: it is set to the one used most.

sections.title: Creating and switching libraries
sections.text: The two arrows icon beside the name opens the quick switch between libraries. In {settings} → Library a new library is created from the field at the top of the section.

sections.title: Managing the selected library
sections.text: Picking a library from the list arms the commands above it: export, rename and set as main.

sections.title: Deleting a library
sections.text: Deleting a library removes only its list: the audio files are left untouched.

transfer.title: Importing and exporting
transfer.figure: The import and export section of the settings.
transfer.tip: To carry the library to another computer, the file is exported and imported on the other installation: the paths still have to lead to the same audio files.

sections.title: Saving a library
sections.text: "Export library" saves a file with the list of tracks and their data, covers included.

sections.title: Importing a library
sections.text: Importing a library asks how to merge it: replace the open one, add only the new tracks, or update the ones already there as well. A summary then says how many tracks entered, how many were updated, how many skipped and which files could not be found.

sections.title: Exporting a list
sections.text: "Export list" saves instead a text or CSV file with the chosen fields: it is meant to be read elsewhere. An exported list holds no audio: it only refers to where the files sit on disk.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.tip: If the interface feels heavy on a slow machine, turning the glass effect and the ambient background off lightens the drawing.

sections.title: Readability and theme
sections.text: Text size: four steps, from very small to large, scaling the whole interface. Theme: light, dark, or the one of the system.

sections.title: Colors and surfaces
sections.text: Accent colour: the colour of the controls, of the selection and of the gradient background. Background and glass: turns on the gradient built from the accent, picks its shape and its origin, and makes the surfaces translucent. It can be carried onto the detail windows too.

sections.title: Player background
sections.text: Background colour from the cover: the player takes its colour from the cover of the track; transparency, intensity, blur, shape and origin are all adjustable. Every choice applies at once and is remembered for the next time.

settings.title: Startup, window and general
settings.figure: The gear in the title bar, which opens the settings.
settings.tip: Start with the system and start minimised work together: with both on, the app is already waiting in the system tray.

sections.title: Language and startup
sections.text: Language: Italian, English, French, Spanish and German, applied immediately. Startup and window: start the app with the system, start minimized in the system tray, and stay there on close instead of quitting. From the tray a click reopens the window, a right click offers to stop the playback or to quit.

sections.title: Player preferences
sections.text: Player: keeps the player open after the track is closed, and sets the floating player — when it appears, whether it stays on top, its layout and what closing it does. Default audio player: on Windows it opens the system settings to associate audio files with this app; on Linux the association belongs to the desktop environment, and the section shows the command to run.

sections.title: About the app
sections.text: The "i" button in the title bar opens the about window: version, website, project on GitHub, release notes and published releases.

storage.title: Original files and app data
storage.where: everywhere; the cover cache is in {settings} → Library.
storage.tip: Emptying the cover cache loses nothing: the covers are read from the files again when they are next needed.

sections.title: Original files
sections.text: Importing files does not copy them: they are read where they sit, and are neither moved nor renamed. The library keeps only the reference to their place. Taking a track out of the list, like deleting a library, deletes nothing from the disk.

sections.title: Metadata changes
sections.text: Saving the metadata updates the tags in the audio file. A replacement cover is written into the file as well.

sections.title: Cover cache
sections.text: {settings} → Library shows how much space the covers use and clears the cache.
